entities.summary:
A Bachelor of Engineering or a Bachelor of Science in Engineering (BSE) is an undergraduate academic degree awarded to a college graduate majoring in an engineering discipline at a higher education institution. First introduced in the United States in 1900, this degree has become a cornerstone of modern technological advancement, shaping the careers of countless engineers who have contributed to innovations in fields such as aerospace, computing, and energy. The Bachelor of Engineering degree has also had a profound impact on the global economy, with graduates playing key roles in driving economic growth and development. As the field of engineering continues to evolve, the Bachelor of Engineering degree remains a vital component of modern higher education, equipping students with the knowledge and skills necessary to tackle complex technical challenges.

The Bachelor of Engineering degree has a rich history, dating back to the early 20th century when the first engineering programs were established in the United States. Initially, these programs were focused on training engineers in specific fields such as mechanical, electrical, and civil engineering. Over time, the degree has evolved to include a broader range of disciplines, including computer science, aerospace engineering, and environmental engineering. Today, the Bachelor of Engineering degree is offered by universities and colleges around the world, with graduates going on to work in a wide range of industries and sectors.
